Cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome-3 (CFC3) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the MEK1 gene (MAP2K1; 176872) on chromosome 15q22.

The protein encoded by this gene is a member of the dual specificity protein kinase family, which acts as a mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinase kinase. This protein kinase lies upstream of MAP kinases and stimulates the enzymatic activity of MAP kinases upon a wide variety of extra- and intracellular signals. # MAP2K1 (MEK1) Functional and Clinical Information

## Function
MAP2K1 serves as a dual specificity protein kinase essential to the MAPK/ERK signaling cascade. It phosphorylates both threonine and tyrosine residues within ERK1/ERK2, activating these downstream kinases. The protein also "activates BRAF in a KSR1 or KSR2-dependent manner" by releasing inhibitory intramolecular interactions that promote scaffolding protein-BRAF dimerization.

## Catalytic Activity
The kinase catalyzes phosphorylation of serine, threonine, and tyrosine residues on protein substrates using ATP as a phosphate donor. Three distinct catalytic reactions are documented:
- Serine phosphorylation (EC 2.7.12.2)
- Threonine phosphorylation (EC 2.7.12.2)
- Tyrosine phosphorylation (EC 2.7.12.2)

## Activation Loop Phosphorylation Sites
Two critical serines enable kinase activation: **Ser-218** and **Ser-222**. These are phosphorylated by BRAF and RAF1 to positively regulate catalytic activity. Additionally, Ser-218 undergoes autophosphorylation promoted by NEK10 following UV damage.

## Disease Associations
- **Cardiofaciocutaneous Syndrome 3 (CFC3)**: Germline mutations cause heart defects, distinctive facial features, and intellectual disability
- **Melorheostosis, Isolated (MEL)**: Somatic mutations produce a sclerosing bone disorder with cortical hyperostosis affecting tubular bones

Based on the web search results, here's comprehensive information about the MEK1 activation loop and its role in the RAF/MEK/ERK pathway:

## MEK1 Activation Loop and Serine 218/222 Phosphorylation

RAF phosphorylates and activates the dual-specificity kinases MEK1/2 at Ser218/Ser222 of MEK1 and Ser222/Ser226 of MEK2. MEK1/2 are activated through serine phosphorylation at the MAPKK-typical Ser-Xaa-Ala-Xaa-Ser/Thr motif in their activation loop (residues 218-222 in human MEK1).

## Structural Changes Upon Activation

The activation loop in the large lobe dramatically changes its inactive versus active orientations in response to Raf-mediated phosphorylation of the two serine residues (i.e., Ser218/222 for MEK1 and Ser222/226 for MEK2). In the inactive conformation, the aspartate side chain (Asp208/212 of MEK1/2) of the conserved DFG sequence in the activation segment faces away from the active site, which is called the "DFG-out" conformation, whereas this aspartate side chain faces into the active site in the active conformation, which is called the "DFG-in" conformation.

## MEK1/2 Phosphorylation of ERK1/2 TEY Motif

MEK1/2 then sequentially phosphorylate Tyr and Thr residues in the TEY site (Thr202/Tyr204 of ERK1; Thr185/Tyr187 of ERK2) of the activation loop of their only known physiological substrates, the serine/threonine kinases ERK1/2.

## Dual-Specificity Nature

MEK1/2 is a dual-specificity protein kinase, classified as part of the serine/threonine protein kinase family, which is capable of catalyzing the phosphorylation of select threonine and tyrosine residues of ERK1/2. Active MEK1/2 phosphorylates ERK on both a tyrosine and threonine residue on the TEY motif of ERK1/2.

A lower Chronos score indicates a higher likelihood that the gene of interest is essential in a given cell line. More specifically, a score of 0 indicates a gene is not essential; correspondingly -1 is comparable to the median of all pan-essential genes.

# MAP2K1 (MEK1, UniProt Q02750) / MAP2K2 (MEK2, UniProt P36507) — Drug Target Research Summary

## Disease Associations

**Somatic cancer mutations:**
- **Melanoma & lung adenocarcinoma**: recurrent MAP2K1 mutations reported, generally mutually exclusive with BRAF V600E; drive MAPK pathway activation independent of upstream RAS/RAF [UniProt Q02750](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q02750/entry).
- **Colorectal cancer**: MAP2K1 hotspot mutations (K57E/N/T, Q56P) in ~1–2% of cases, mutually exclusive with RAS/RAF mutations, associated with poor response to anti-EGFR therapy [Clin Colorectal Cancer 2020](https://www.clinical-colorectal-cancer.com/article/S1533-0028(20)30171-7/fulltext); also reported in papillary thyroid cancer [PMC8144646](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8144646/).
- **Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH)**: MAP2K1 mutations found in ~33% of BRAF-wild-type LCH lesions, mutually exclusive with BRAF V600E, supporting ERK activation as the central LCH driver [Blood 2014, Nelson et al.](https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/124/19/3007/33329); confirmed in a separate cohort [Blood 2014, Brown et al.](https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/124/10/1655/32977).
- **Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD)**: BRAF V600E in 57–70%, MAP2K1 mutations in ~20% [CancerNetwork case report](https://www.cancernetwork.com/view/erdheim-chester-disease-a-case-report-of-braf-v600e-negative-map2k1-positive-ecd-diagnosed-by-blood-next-generation-sequencing-assay-and-a-brief-literature-review).
- **Melorheostosis** (isolated sclerosing bone disorder): somatic activating MAP2K1 mutations [UniProt Q02750](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q02750/entry).

**Germline (RASopathy):** Heterozygous MAP2K1 mutations cause **Cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome-3 (CFC3)** (~9.8% of CFC cases; distinguishing features include macrostomia and horizontal palpebral fissures) [OMIM 176872](https://omim.org/entry/176872), [OMIM 615279](https://omim.org/entry/615279). The paralog MAP2K2 similarly causes **CFC4** [OMIM 615280](https://omim.org/entry/615280); other CFC subtypes arise from BRAF (CFC1) and KRAS (CFC2).

## Mechanism

MEK1/2 sit in the canonical **RAS→RAF→MEK→ERK** cascade. RAF kinases (BRAF/RAF1) phosphorylate MEK1 at activation-loop **Ser218/Ser222** (MEK2: Ser222/Ser226), driving a DFG-out→DFG-in conformational switch that activates the kinase [UniProt](https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q02750.txt); [MDPI review 2020](https://www.mdpi.com/1422-0067/21/15/5436). Active MEK1/2 is a **dual-specificity kinase** that phosphorylates the TEY activation motif of ERK1/2 (Thr202/Tyr204 in ERK1; Thr185/Tyr187 in ERK2), the only known physiological substrates [PMC4663016, MEK1/2 inhibitor resistance review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4663016/). MEK1 also feeds back to activate BRAF via KSR1/2 scaffolding [UniProt](https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q02750.txt).

Oncogenic hotspots cluster in the **exon 2 negative-regulatory region** (F53del, Q56P, K57E/N) and **exon 3 catalytic core** (C121S, E203K), producing "class II," partially RAF-independent, constitutively active MEK1 [High-throughput functional study, PMC9890140](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9890140/). **C121S** confers resistance to both BRAF and MEK inhibitors (including trametinib) [PMC9890140](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9890140/); **E203K** confers resistance to cobimetinib and to anti-PD-1 checkpoint blockade, yet remains trametinib-sensitive [Leng et al., Chin Clin Oncol 2025](https://cco.amegroups.org/article/view/132758/html).

**MAP2K2/MEK2 (P36507)** is a paralog (~80% identity) with an analogous mechanism and activation-loop residues (Ser222/Ser226); its germline mutations cause CFC4, and MEK1/MEK2 mutations can co-occur as acquired BRAF-inhibitor resistance mechanisms in melanoma.

**Bottom line for target assessment**: MEK1/2 are validated, druggable nodes (multiple approved MEK inhibitors exist — trametinib, cobimetinib, binimetinib) with clear oncogenic and germline (RASopathy) genetics, but resistance mutations (C121S, E203K) are a known liability for any new inhibitor chemotype targeting this node.

# MAP2K1 (MEK1) — DepMap Dependency & Drug Sensitivity Summary

**1. CRISPR Essentiality**

MAP2K1 is not classified as a common (pan-)essential gene in DepMap's genome-wide CRISPR screens (Chronos/CERES scores, ~1,000+ lines); it does not clear the ~-0.5 to -1 common-essential threshold across the panel. Instead, it behaves as a **selective/context-dependent** vulnerability, with strongest gene-effect scores concentrated in **BRAF-mutant** lines. Pan-cancer dependency analyses (e.g., the SuperDendrix framework applied to DepMap CERES data) found MAP2K1 dependency, alongside MAPK1, MITF, and DUSP4, significantly enriched in **BRAF-activating-mutant lines, particularly cutaneous melanoma**, consistent with earlier reports of conditional MAP2K1 essentiality specifically in BRAF(V600E) melanoma models ([PMC8979493](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8979493/); [depmap.org/portal/gene/MAP2K1](https://depmap.org/portal/gene/MAP2K1?tab=overview)). Sanger's **Project Score** (323 lines, 19 tissue types; drug data cross-linked to GDSC) similarly frames MAP2K1 as a lineage-selective MAPK-pathway dependency rather than universal essential gene ([academic.oup.com/nar D1365](https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/49/D1/D1365/5929235); [score.depmap.sanger.ac.uk](https://score.depmap.sanger.ac.uk/gene/MAP2K1)). Notably, combinatorial/paralog CRISPR screening identified **MAP2K1–MAP2K2 as a synthetic-lethal paralog pair**, i.e., co-dependency between MEK1/MEK2 emerges even where single-gene knockout effects are modest — a key tractability signal for dual MEK1/2 inhibition ([bioRxiv 2026.01.19.700065](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.01.19.700065v1.full)).

**2. Drug Sensitivity**

GDSC/CTRP/PRISM have profiled multiple MEK1/2 inhibitors (trametinib, selumetinib/AZD6244, PD0325901, RDEA119/refametinib, binimetinib, cobimetinib) across >1,000 lines ([cancerrxgene.org](https://www.cancerrxgene.org/); [pubmed 23180760](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23180760/)). Pattern: **BRAF-mutant lines (melanoma, colorectal) show greatest sensitivity**, **NRAS-mutant lines intermediate**, and **KRAS-mutant lines least sensitive on average** (higher mean IC50) ([GDSC, PMC3531057](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3531057/)). A cluster of 41 NRAS-mutant lines was commonly responsive to PD0325901, trametinib, and selumetinib. Clinically, MAP2K1 "class 2" (RAF-regulated) mutants are most MEK-inhibitor-responsive, while class-3 (RAF-independent) mutants confer resistance ([PMC9890140](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9890140/); trametinib resistance case, [pubmed 36901951](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36901951/)).

**Bottom line for target assessment:** MEK1/2 is a validated, tractable target — selectively essential (not pan-essential) with strong genotype-defined (BRAF/RAS) vulnerability and multiple approved/clinical-stage inhibitors, supporting biomarker-guided rather than universal targeting.
